2.5.1.5-f1.accuracy_reason: Horace, Odes 2.11.17–18 reads 'dissipat Euhius / curas edacis'. The gloss of Euius as Bacchus and the misprint 'edates' for 'edaces' are both right.

2.5.1.5-f27.accuracy_reason: The line is Martial 10.48.14, from the dinner-menu epigram. Burton's sidenote gives only 'Mart.', so the claim that he gives no locus is fair.

2.5.1.5-f37.accuracy_reason: 'Ebrietas est blandus daemon, dulce venenum' is commonly attributed to Augustine (probably pseudo-Augustine), and the note properly hedges on the source.

2.5.1.5-f5.accuracy_reason: Tibullus 1.7.41–42 reads 'crura licet dura compede pulsa sonent', as the note quotes.

2.5.1.5-f8.accuracy_reason: De tranquillitate animi 17.12 closes with 'Habes, Serene carissime, quae possint tranquillitatem tueri, quae restituere…'. The note quotes this correctly, and Serenus is the man the work is addressed to.

2.5.1.5-f9.accuracy_reason: Both loci are correct: Odes 3.28.2–3 and Epodes 9.33–34.
